Please go ahead and share any relevant findings on the equipment, software platform, funding, and installation timeline.

transcript.text: I should share an important finding from my classroom trial. I conducted a trial this week with the enrolled section, and the results show that all 12 students need simultaneous stations — that's one laptop and one USB microphone per student. I recorded these results in my classroom planning log, but I should note the log was not attached to the capital request proposal. Based on this trial, the draft proposal's request for 10 laptops would be insufficient for the 12 enrolled students.

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Monroe. I'd like to share my findings from the network and privacy review I completed this week. The commercial cloud platform requested in the draft proposal cannot be used with student accounts under our district privacy and security policies. However, our district-managed SoundLab EDU platform is approved and supports student use — it requires managed student accounts and a security configuration record on file. I did close the technology review ticket this week, but I want to flag that the ticket has not yet been linked to the purchasing request, so we should make sure that connection is documented before finalizing.

transcript.text: I have an important funding finding to report. I received the Arts Innovation Grant award notice this week and filed it in the business-office grant folder. The grant will fund this project, but only up to exactly $6,800 — not the $8,000 requested in the draft proposal. Additionally, the grant requires that the purchase order be issued by August 20, 2026. Under the grant's purchasing sequence, the purchase order must be followed by procurement and setup, which means September 15, 2026 is the earliest feasible installation date — not the September 1, 2026 date in the draft proposal. I should also note that the grant funding information has not yet been added to the proposal.
